newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's FCL Forest, Building, Energy gain post-result.
newsitem.headline: NZ's FCL Forest, Building, Energy gain post-result.

text.p: The share prices of Fletcher Energy, Building and Forests all gained after reporting their June year results on Wednesday.
The odd man out was Paper, which lost ground.

Analysts said that while many of the numbers were out of kilter with forecasts, due in part to various tax treatments, the earnings before interest and tax were broadly in line with expectations for all four of the "letter" stocks.
David Stanley at Doyle Paterson Brown said most of the businesses performed in line with expectations.
Tax provisions, in several instances, were lower, especially for Forests, he said.
Building enjoyed a greater tax benefit from the losses associated with some overseas businesses than the market was anticipating. Provisions for tax were higher than expected for Paper.
"But overall you would have to say the market would have been expecting pretty much what the numbers were that came through, both pre-abnormals and post-abnormals," Stanley said.

Campbell Johnstone at Hendry Hay McIntosh said the market, by and large, liked the results. "But Paper appears to be under a bit of pressure." FCL Paper made cautious comments about its key markets, pulp and paper, which are still depressed.

By 12.45 p.m. (0030 GMT) Energy was up nine cents at NZ$3.40 -- its highest point since splitting as a letter stock in March. Forests firmed five to NZ$$2.05 and Building gained eight to NZ$3.27. Paper lost eight cents to NZ$2.78.
The movements took place in a stronger market overall, the NZSE-40 Capital Index gaining 18.20 points to 2,237.27 by midday.
FCL Paper said conditions for printing papers and market pulp were expected to remain dificult for at least the first half of the current year to June 1997.
It reported a NZ$177 million net profit for the year to June 1996, up three percent on the previous year.
FCL Energy said earnings and cash flow were expected to rise as the Maui F Sands oil comes into full production in October.
The Canadian operations would build on their quality assets to grow production, cashflow and returns, FCL Energy said.

In Brunei, where it has secured offshore exploration rights to 800 square kilometres, the Maharaja Lela 3 well was spudded in May with hydrocarbons, both oil and gas, being encountered in a number of reservoir sequences. If the project proceeds, production could be expected within two years.
Energy announced a net profit of NZ$57 million against $64 million a year earlier.
FCL Building said it was confident New Zealand housing starts were set to rise after a decline in 1996. Its profit came in at NZ$121 million, up from $117 million.
